newsitem.title: USA: CME traders say USDA pork data neutral for futures.
newsitem.headline: CME traders say USDA pork data neutral for futures.

text.p: Traders at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said U.S. Agriculture Department cold storage data for pork should not affect CME lean hog or pork belly futures Monday.
Traders said the USDA pork storage figures were slightly greater than expected but the bullish news Thursday that Taiwan will suspend pork exports will override the bearish impact of the USDA report.
"What would have been a bearish figure...has been muted by the events of the past 24 hours," said Chuck Levitt, analyst with Alaron Trading Corp.

USDA reported there 43.881 million lbs of frozen bellies in storage February 28, slightly more than the 41.2 million to 43 million that analysts had estimated. Also, total U.S. frozen pork supplies as of February 28 were 387.027 million lbs up from 344.483 million a month earlier.
Levitt said the suspension of Taiwan pork exports due to a foot and mouth disease outbreak there should boost export demand for U.S. pork and mean higher prices for U.S. hogs.
"It is going to add $5 (per cwt) to the value (of hogs) between now and summer," he said of the increased demand for U.S. pork to replace Taiwan pork on the world market.
